**Finding: missing (insurance clause absent) — redline proposed and validated.**

Summary of the investigation:

- **Search and full read confirmed the gap.** A literal search for "insurance" returned zero hits, and reading the entire agreement (one section, p0000–p0074) found no coverage obligation on either party and no Exhibit reference to insurance.
- **The rule applies here.** Kubient is squarely a services/hosting vendor touching our data: it hosts the Auction Platform (p0002), receives Request data from AP (p0011), and warrants that it collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information/data (p0035). Under the rule, no insurance for a vendor processing personal data is walk-away territory, not a fallback — so this is a genuine missing-clause finding rather than a rationale-only note.
- **Direction check.** The inserted obligation binds Kubient (the counterparty) and benefits AP, so there is no risk of flagging something in our own favor.
- **Placement and size.** The edit is a single new subsection 14(j) inserted after p0073, at the end of General Provisions, consistent with the redline guidance to keep it short and in the miscellaneous section. No existing text is altered.
- **Limits.** Drafted at the preferred position (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where our or visitor data is processed, workers' comp as required by law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) expressly offered in the comment as a negotiating concession — appropriate given this is a low-severity, revenue-share arrangement.

One judgment call worth flagging for you: I broadened the cyber trigger to "Customer or visitor data" rather than the model language's "Customer Data," because this agreement has no defined term "Customer Data" and the data Kubient actually handles is described as visitor information. If your house style prefers tracking the model wording verbatim, that phrase is the only place it departs.
